MC cause of lrg bowel obstruct in adults
▪︎2nd MC cause of cancer death in US after lung; untreated fatal in ~50%
•diet (↓fiber, ↑in red or processed meat, animal fat)
•also: hx of adenomatous polyps, DM, radiation exposure
▪︎75% no known predisposing factors; men higher mortality than women
: physical activity, regular use of ASA, NSAIDs
– almost all will develop colon CA by age 45yrs; prophylactic colectomy best for survival
▪︎classic FAP (AKA polyposis coli): AD; 100s-1,000s of colorectal adenomas; ~100% CRC risk if ⍉tx (CA by age 40)
▪︎at risk: 1st-degree relatives w/ FAP; >10 cumulative colorectal adenomas
▪︎APC = tumor suppressor; loss ⇢ beta-catenin accum ⇢ aberrant Wnt signaling ⇢ uncontrolled epithelial proliferation
▪︎classic: multiple polyps by teenage yrs, early CRC (~39); attenuated: 10-99 polyps, proximal colon, later CRC (~56)
▪︎extracolonic: duodenal adenomas (2nd leading cause of death), desmoid tumors, thyroid CA (papillary, cribriform-morular)
▪︎ASx until CA develops; presymptomatic dx essential
▪︎most CRC sporadic (rest: familial risk, Lynch, FAP, hamartomatous polyposis)
: AD; d/t loss of funct in DNA mismatch repair genes (
); 40% risk of colon CA – mean age late 40s
▪︎Lynch = germline mutation of DNA mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) or EPCAM deletion; MC cause of inherited CRC
▪︎also assoc: gastric, small intestine, endometrial, ovarian, urinary tract, skin, pancreatic CA
▪︎Lynch: Rt-sided, lrg tumors, rapid development, mean age 44 vs FAP: slower, bowel-constricting, mean 16; Lynch polyps absent/few
(lips, oral mucosa, hands) – risk of breast/pancreatic CA
(fatigue, weakness), rectal bleed, abd pain, Δ in bowel habits
▪︎may be aSx early; can cause hematochezia or melena
▪︎nonpolypoid neoplasms ↑ risk of CA vs polypoid; bleeding mass protruding into lumen = classic
, (CRC = MC cause of occult GI bleed in adults)
▪︎CEA ⍉for dx or screening; obtain after dx & monitor serially after tx
•flexible sigmoidoscopy q5yrs + fecal occult blood testing q3yrs
•screening works: polyp → CA over 8-10yrs & curable if caught early
▪︎1st-degree relative w/ CRC → screen 10yrs before relative's dx age (father dx @53 → screen @43); relative w/ advanced polyp → colonoscopy @40 or 10yrs before their dx
▪︎USPSTF grades: A = high certainty substantial net benefit; B = moderate certainty ≥moderate net benefit; age 76-85 = grade C (case-by-case); ⍉screen >85yo
▪︎also: sDNA-FIT (Cologuard) q3yrs; flex sig q5yrs + FIT q1yr
▪︎hereditary CRC syndromes, IBD, CF, abdominopelvic radiation → may screen <45yo
▪︎RF (smoke, red/processed meat, ↓fiber, ETOH, DM, obesity, IBD) ⍉alter screening recs
▪︎Amsterdam criteria (3-2-1): 3 family members w/ Lynch-assoc CA, ≥2 generations, ≥1 dx <50yo
▪︎revised Bethesda guidelines ⇢ tumor testing for microsatellite instability in Lynch-assoc CRC
▪︎Lynch mgmt: regular endometrial & ovarian screening; surg resection; chemo
: lifelong annual colonoscopy beginning 12yrs until colectomy

▪︎FAP colectomy indications: suspected CRC, severe Sx (ex, GI bleed), adenomas w/ high-grade dysplasia, multiple adenomas >6mm, ↑ # polyps on consecutive colonoscopies, or can't adequately visualize d/t multiple diminutive polyps
▪︎FAP surgery: total proctocolectomy w/ ileal pouch anal anastomosis (IPAA) or total colectomy w/ ileorectal anastomosis; IPAA for profuse polyposis, >10 rectal adenomas, or ↑ desmoid risk
▪︎postcolectomy: endoscopy of rectum & ileal pouch q1-2yrs (CA risk from anal transition zone or ileal pouch)
